question: How should GA display uncertainty and rate resolution for a small historical chatbot QA suite without inventing a confidence interval?
production_path: investigation: observe hypothesize test conclude reflect
hypothesis: Showing count-based step size and category denominators may make a 98.08% headline easier to interpret without suggesting unjustified statistical confidence.
evidence: GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924: state/quality/chatbot-qa/2026-06-15.json reports 75.0% of 52; state/quality/chatbot-qa/2026-07-19.json reports 98.08% of 52.
The same July snapshot reports operations 85.71% of 7, getting-started 100% of 1, and modes 100% of 13; it omits prompt IDs and evaluator revision.
Arithmetic checks: 39/52=75%; 51/52 rounds to 98.08%; one changed verdict is 100/52=1.923 percentage points overall and 100/7=14.286 in operations.
Research duration was not instrumented; duration_seconds=0 records that limitation.
